dsc: The Ambulance (1977) (also listed as 1978 or 1979 in various sources, and listed as "Chevy Ambulance" in 1999 to distinguish it from the "Ford Ambulance" in that year's line up) is actually two very similar castings. The first casting (41-C) was released for 1978 (with a 1977 copyright), and was retired in 1981 or 1982. The second casting (25-E) was released in 1983, with minor variations in the base, and appeared steadily in the Superfast 1-75 lineup through 1991. This second casting retains the 1977 copyright date, and appeared sporadically through 1999, sometimes only in multi-packs. Taken together, the castings reflect important changes at Matchbox and in ambulance design.

dsc: *The Ambulance (2000) is a fantasy ambulance, featuring opening rear doors. A patient (loaded backwards) is visible in the rear compartment, making this the first (and so far only) ambulance casting featuring a molded-in-place patient. The casting reflects the short-lived early 21st century shift away from realism that marked many of the then-introduced Matchbox models. When the company direction changed again, this casting was retired in favor of the more realistic Ambulance (2005).

dsc: The Articulated Truck is a three-axle tractor-trailer combination, offered in the 1-75 range and later included in the Twin Packs range with a second trailer. The tractor features a ball and post which fits a socket in the trailer. Though the tractor unit is shared with the Freeway Gas Tanker, and is therefore interchangeable with that model, this seems to be for manufacturing reasons, rather than for play value. Wheel type sometimes varied between the tractor and trailer, even on models packaged together. Colored glazing, a small cab, and no rear window space hide the lack of an interior. The Twin Packs version was introduced in 1978.

dsc: The Ford LTD sports a light bar on its roof. The model has a noteworthy lightbar design, the lightbar being attached from the inside of the car body, but not being part of the window plastic. This allows the lightbar and the windows to be different colors, while the lightbar cannot become detached during hard play. In some versions, the two halves of the lightbar are different colors, which for other models is not possible without the use of paint, or gluing two differently-colored lightbar halves together. This design was also used for the Plymouth Gran Fury of 1979, and with the beacons on several earlier emergency vehicles.

dsc: *The Leyland Cabover Cab is a model of a tractor cab, the second in the 900 series after Long Haul, first issued in 1981 in the 900 series as TP-2 with Tanker Trailer and TP-26 with Low Bed Trailer unit with boat. Officially it was called only "Articulated Truck", but the recognizable form based on the Leyland T45. Later therefore called it Leyland Cabover Cab, possibly Leyland Tractor. The truck come with two colors, red in TP-2 with Tanker Trailer and blue in TP-26 with Boat Trailer. The Leyland Cabover Cab career was short, 1983 Matchbox launched the Convoy range, but the Leyland truck did not continue manufacturing it.

dsc: The Long Haul is a model of a tractor cab, first issued in 1979 in the 900 series as TP-22, TP23, TP24 & TP25, each with an articulated trailer unit. Articulated trucks with removable cabs had previously been issued in the 1-75 Series and had also been released in the Accesory Packs, Major Packs, King Size and Super Kings ranges, but the Long Haul may be the first Matchbox tractor cab which was intended to function both with and without a trailer, and to be swapped among multiple trailers.

dsc: The first-generation shipping container, also known as the P. S. I Container, was designed to fit onto certain Matchbox vehicles of the late 1970s. Slots in the container's side accept the lifting prongs of the Sambron Jacklift, allowing that truck to lift the container and move it between other vehicles. Holes in the bottom accept short pegs on the Mercedes-Benz Container Truck, helping to hold the container in place. A low ridge around the edge of other vehicles served the same purpose. Neither mechanism held the container very strongly, however, and the shipping container often fell off of its vehicle during all but the most gentle play.

dsc: The K-32/40 Shovel Nose is a King Size fantasy Matchbox vehicle, featuring a wedge-like shape, oversized rear wheels, and an opening cockpit. It appeared in yellow, as a race car (K-32); and in red, as a fire chief's car (K-40). In both cases, the base is marked "K-32/40 Shovel Nose", but packaging for the red version identified it as Blaze Trailer.

dsc: The Streakers have been a subseries within the 1-75 basic range between 1975-1980. 10 cars were given colorful tampo print decoration on their base color. The models also received new packaging too. However, their serial number remained unchanged. Some racetracks have been similarly modified, which have also been given the name Streakers. In the 2000s, some re-released models in the new Superfast range also received the paint and name typical of the series.

dsc: *Matchbox Two Packs (stylized as "Two" Packs) originated in 1976. They featured two vehicles in a single box or blister pack. Some vehicles were the same as those then available in the 1-75 range, while others were special editions. Once the 1-75 range split into INT and USA versions, "Two" Packs sometimes featured vehicles from the other line, e.g. an INT vehicle in the USA market. Sets were numbered with a TP- prefix under all series names.
